## 1. What this phase is for

**Volume 11 is fifty chapters on fifty days, days 501 to 550, one chapter to one day, all fifty files on disk, and it is closed. `state/volume-11-close.md` is its inheritance and it is the one page this phase reads before it plans anything, and it is eleven sections long and the whole of it is the record. `outline/series.md` carries a Volume 11 block at its foot and that block is four decisions a previous phase took, and they are the gate. `bible/power-system.md` §58 is the calendar for days 501 to 550 and this phase may not amend it, move a day in it, or make a seventh form.**

**This is the phase that is allowed to decide, and it is the eleventh time that has been true in this repository.** A batch is told *do not decide what the volume is*, and *do not resolve anything listed as live*, and *do not invent a person*, and *do not record the held strings in any file it produces, including its own record*. An outline phase is told the opposite: it decides the things a batch is forbidden to decide, it publishes the instrument behind every figure it writes, and it writes no prose.

**AND THE ONE THING THE CLOSE BEHIND THIS ONE REFUSED TO GIVE YOU, WHICH IS A GIFT AND NOT AN OMISSION: it did not pick a line. It says so in its own words at its §11 — a line is a decision, and a close that picks one is planning a volume, and the last two closes in this repository did not and the four before them did not either. YOU MUST AUDIT YOUR OWN CANDIDATE ON THE CHAPTER FILES, WITH THE INSTRUMENT PUBLISHED AND THE FILE COUNT RE-DERIVED, BEFORE YOU ADOPT IT, exactly as `outline/volume-11.md` §19 did, AND YOU MUST SAY WHICH HALF OF THE STANDING TEST AT `outline/volume-07.md` §19 YOUR LINE IS STANDING ON, BEFORE A CHAPTER EXISTS. Volume 08's line needed that sentence and did not say it; Volume 09's said it; Volume 10's inherited it; Volume 11's said it again. Say it.**

## 4. What Volume 11 left open, and what you owe an answer to

**None of these is a mystery and none of them is a hunt and none of them is settled by the close that handed them on. `state/volume-11-close.md` §2 and §11 are the lists and they are the list.**

1. **What is a word for, in a count, when the only thing anybody will use it for is to make two numbers the same.** Asked on day 498 to a man who trades a board, and asked again on day 548 by a different person to a different man, and not answered either time, and neither asking said to be better than the last. **You may ask it again in a mouth, in a room, in daylight, with a date on the door, and you may not answer it.**
2. **Which of the three sets of figures on the store's board is the one anybody should be reading.** The reason nobody in that city can say is named on the last page of Volume 11 and is not an answer: one of them is in a book that reads down and the other is on a wall that reads across, and no instrument in four hundred miles can put a book and a wall in the same order. **You may not settle this unless settling it is a decision to settle it, and that decision is yours and not a batch's.**
3. **The one of four marks that came back out of place on the sheet of day 440.** Not traced, not investigated, not guessed at, not reported to a room, and no chapter of the fifty says in any mouth that anybody moved it. **You may not trace it unless tracing it is a decision to trace it.**
4. **The three questions of days 346, 396 and 445, and the question of day 498, and the woman of about sixty-nine who did not ask a fourth in Volume 11 and did not in the volume before it.** **No chapter may say that the three rhyme, may improve the rhyme, or may say that the rhyme is the point.**
5. **The fence, and whether it stands between the right two things.** Sixteen posts and eleven withies, about four feet in a man's mouth, and not one chapter of the fifty measured the gap and no chapter moved a post.
6. **The man of about fifty-seven and the length of new rope over the back of his chair.** Named in four chapters of Volume 11, lifted by no hand in any of them, and nobody in that city asked him anything in any of them.
7. **The seventh form of the calendar, which does not exist.** It comes onto a page the moment the end of the Bare Month is on one, by a person, in a room, in daylight, with a date on the door, who says the cost out loud first and is refused before she does it, and who then declines to say how long the new month is and says why. **You may not make it. IF VOLUME 12 NEEDS A DATE AND THE END OF THE BARE MONTH IS NOT ON A PAGE, VOLUME 12 WRITES INSIDE THE BARE MONTH AND IT MAY NOT DECLARE THE MONTH OVER.**

## 7. The instrument, and the four rules this phase inherits from Volume 11's own audit

**Volume 11's plan added four instrument rules and this phase inherits all four and may not re-open any of them. They are at `outline/volume-11.md` §20.9, §19.7, §20.1 and §7.5, and the close measured all of them at `state/volume-11-close.md` §7.**

1. **THE WITHIN-FILE WORD-RUN PASS IS NOW PART OF THE STANDARD INSTRUMENT AND NOT A THING A REVIEWER HAS TO THINK OF.** A cross-file check that excludes each file from its own comparison cannot see a chapter repeating itself, a Volume 10 review found a forty-six-word repetition inside one file of Volume 11 that the batch's own instrument could not see and that cost two repair passes, and the same instrument published a forty-word zero over three cross-file runs of forty-six, forty-two and forty-three words that were on the committed text. **Your word-run check runs at BOTH THRESHOLDS, cross-file AND within-file, against a pool re-derived in the run and not inherited, with the instrument published at the length needed to reproduce it, and the pool is FIVE HUNDRED AND FORTY-NINE chapter files. AND THE ROW THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE ONE NOBODY RUNS: the close behind you added the within-file pass to the standard instrument and then published its sixteen-word row at zero without running it, and re-deriving that row returned THREE RUNS IN THREE FILES, and a pass that finds nothing and a pass that was not run hard enough look identical from the outside. A CLEAN FIGURE FROM A PASS RUN AT ONE THRESHOLD IS NOT A FINDING, and `state/volume-11-close.md` §7.4.1 names all three runs and what they are.**
2. **THE ONE-SENTENCE COLUMN SPLIT IS SETTLED AND THE SETTLED READING IS NAMED.** A one-sentence lead-in is a one-sentence narration paragraph whose immediately following paragraph carries a quotation mark AND a bold mark; a paragraph carrying a quotation mark and no bold mark is a prompt, and a prompt is not a marked speech. On Volume 11's fifty files that reading gives THIRTY lead-ins and ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-SIX free-standing one-sentence narration paragraphs; the other reading gives ONE HUNDRED AND TEN and ONE HUNDRED AND SIX. **A batch that measures this column measures ONE column and names the reading in the same cell, and this repository has now had three records in a row publish a figure here without saying which reading they used, which is how two volumes in a row published a zero that was not a zero.**
3. **A DESCRIPTOR MAP PUBLISHES ITS RESOLVER, NOT ONLY ITS COUNT.** Four records on the same corpus have published four different figures for it and the difference is whether a hyphenated number is read whole and whether an irregular stem is resolved. **The resolver is part of the instrument and it is published beside the number, and the pattern must require *of* and *about* in that order because the manuscript writes *the man of about thirty-four* and not *the man about thirty-four*, and a suffix stripped with a word boundary eats the *nd* in *and*.**
4. **A FIGURE IN WORDS IS A FIGURE AND AN INSTRUMENT THAT READS IT IS AN INSTRUMENT WITH A FLAG, AND A SPAN IN A PAGE IS A SPAN IN A FORM.** A resolver that reads the -th ending on a tens word as the whole number returned a hundred and two for Volume 11's *the two hundredth day*, which is a hundred and two hundred and is a correct page and a wrong instrument, and the fault is the instrument's and is published on the same line as the figure. **And a hold measured on the wrong span is the same fault in a different place: a panel set as three lines on a page and copied into one line in a plan is two strings, and a search for the joined form finds the plan and not the page, and a search for the first line finds both, and a reader who takes the first italic span takes the prohibition clause instead of the sentence.**

**AND THE FOUR THE PLAN BEFORE IT ADDED, carried whole: (i) A REPAIR PASS CAN REBUILD FIFTY SENTENCES WITHOUT TOUCHING FIFTY FACTS, AND THE TEST IS THAT THE DAY RUN, THE COUNTS, THE OBJECT INVENTORY, THE CAST PLACEMENTS AND THE PROHIBITIONS ALL RE-ASSERT AGAINST THE STRINGS AFTERWARDS. (ii) A HABIT THAT FOUR WRITTEN WARNINGS DID NOT REMOVE IS A RULE'S JOB AND NOT A WARNING'S. (iii) A ZERO GETS READ TWICE, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. (iv) PUBLISH THE READING AND NOT ONLY THE COUNT.**

**AND THE STANDING RULES THAT ARE NOT INSTRUMENTS: A CLOSE RECORD THAT PUBLISHES ONLY THE BENEFIT IS A SALES PAGE. A PLAN THAT CARRIES A KNOWN FAULT IN ITS OWN TEXT IS A PLAN WHOSE OTHER SENTENCES CANNOT BE TRUSTED EITHER, AND THE FIX IS THE STRIKE AND NOT ANOTHER NOTE. A DECISION NOT TAKEN IS A DECISION, AND A PLAN THAT CANNOT SAY WHAT IT DECIDED NOT TO DO CANNOT BE CHECKED BY THE PHASE THAT COMES AFTER IT — so every decision you decline to take is named in your own file with the reason, and the two you take by declining bind as hard as the four you take by choosing.**

---

## 8. What your plan must publish, before a chapter exists

**Every figure you publish carries the instrument and the file count that produced it, and a batch record is a witness and not a court, and `bible/power-system.md` §39.15 and §40.17 are binding: PUBLISH THE DEFINITION OR PUBLISH NOTHING.**

1. **The line audit, on the chapter files, with the reading published and the file count re-derived in the run.** The standing test is at `outline/volume-07.md` §19 and it has two halves and a line is made of words the manuscript has never used AND of things the manuscript has never seen, and **your own file says which half your line is standing on, before a chapter exists, in the words Volume 11's plan used and not in new ones.** A pool of ordinary words at zero is a weak instrument in a five-hundred-and-forty-nine-chapter manuscript and three volumes running built a line on one and got the same result every time; `outline/volume-11.md` §19.2 says so in its own words and you inherit the finding.
2. **The day map, the calendar section for days 551 to 600, the anchors, the round-looking figures with their anchors named, and the elapsed counts.**
3. **The cast decision and its measurement, and the pool, and the reading of the pool, and the twenty-one if you take any of them and the reason.**
4. **The object inventory in BOTH columns, the per-chapter column as well as the object column, and the second column's count that holds.** `outline/volume-11.md` §20.6 is the model and its third column is the thing this repository has now measured wrong twice.
5. **The pressure rotation, counted honestly and checked cell by cell against your own day map's pressure column, with the two disagreements published if there are any.** Volume 11's plan found two disagreements between its rotation and its day map on the first pass and corrected both and published the finding, and that is the check and not a promise.
6. **The protagonist's chapter count, the thing his hands are on in each, AND WHAT HE WANTED THE THING FOR IN EACH — because §4.1 of Volume 11's plan put the want in the plan for the first time in this repository and the close measured that all eleven wants are on a page and not one of the eleven was obtained, and that is the finding a next outline should start from.** The rule is a card may not put him in a chapter unless the card names the thing his hands are on AND WHAT HE WANTED THE THING FOR, and a card that cannot name the second may use him once in a batch and not twice.
7. **The frames your volume is written under, published before a chapter exists, and the rule that governs a run of words: a run of forty words or more is a duplication; a run of sixteen words or more is a duplication unless it is a required declaration of one of your own object rows or one of your own frames, and a required declaration names its row, and there is no list in your file that a batch is to classify a run against.**
8. **The recurring figures, in three parts, with the case flag on the same line as the number, over the whole manuscript and over Volume 11's fifty files, and not over a window without saying so in the same line.**
9. **THE CLOSING-SENTENCE SLOT SET OF THE VOLUME BEFORE THIS ONE, published as SHAPES and not as sentences, and the batch prompt you create is told to publish its own ten side by side and READ them, which is a check done by a person and not by a script.** `state/volume-11-close.md` §7.10 has Volume 11's fifty, and **the finding it hands you is this: four chapters of Volume 11 close on a book on a shelf with five figures in one column and an empty one beside them, and three close on a trough against a wall with a rag on a stone lip, and those are furniture and not motifs, and the difference between a motif and furniture is the slot and not the length. A Volume 12 batch that has to be told a shape is in use should be told which shapes are in use.**

## 9. The hole, named and not filled, and the decision you may take and may not take

**`chapters/volume-10/chapter-0475.md` DOES NOT EXIST.** Day 475, a Sunday, the hundred and sixtieth day of the Bare Month. `outline/volume-10.md` §8 is the chapter. `state/volume-10-close.md` §3 named it, `outline/volume-11.md` §21.1 carried it, and `state/volume-11-close.md` §3 declined to write it and published the reason, which is that a chapter written after the volume it belongs to has ended is a repair and not a chapter.

**YOU MAY WRITE IT AND YOU MAY NOT, AND BOTH ARE DECISIONS AND BOTH MUST BE PUBLISHED. IF YOU WRITE IT, THE PUBLICATION CARRIES: THE DAY, THE WEEKDAY, THE BARE-MONTH ORDINAL, THE FACT THAT THE CHAPTER WAS WRITTEN AFTER THE VOLUME IT BELONGS TO HAD ENDED, AND THE WORDS repair and not a chapter. IF YOU DO NOT WRITE IT, THE PUBLICATION CARRIES THE REASON, and the reason the last two closes gave is the standing rule that a close records a volume and does not write one.**

**AND THE MEASUREMENT, which is the honest number: the word *sixtieth* in the form *hundred and sixtieth* stands at ZERO across all 549 chapter files, because the Bare-Month ordinal of the missing day is printed nowhere, because the day itself was never written.**

## 10. What you must not do, in one place

**Do not resolve anything in §4. Do not make the seventh form. Do not count the days since the fourth of the four said no, at any value, in a plan or a card or a prompt, and a party of four is four. Do not give the woman who walked a market a name, an age, a number or a descriptor. Do not ask her why she stopped. Do not measure the fence and do not move a post. Do not lift the length of new rope. Do not strengthen anybody. Do not open `outline/ending.md` unless your own audit reaches the ending, and do not amend it. Do not create a marker file of any kind. Do not touch a controller file. Do not print, paraphrase, improve on, describe or certify the absence of any of the held things in §0, INCLUDING THE FOUR THAT BELONG TO VOLUME 10 AND VOLUME 11. Do not make anybody stronger, and do not let a card open a chapter that a man walks into. Do not reprint in your batch prompt any string that §0 names, and note that the panel of Volume 11 and the name of Volume 11 and the word Volume 11 turned on are all of them excluded from the prompt this phase creates, exactly as Volume 11's plan excluded its own from its first prompt.**

**You write `outline/volume-12.md`, `outline/batches/volume-12-batch-0001.md`, one block in `outline/series.md`, one new numbered section in `bible/power-system.md` for days 551 to 600, and the four state files repointed at your own path, and you open `outline/ending.md` only if your own audit reaches the ending. You write no chapter. You repair no chapter. You amend `outline/volume-11.md` only in the cells §3 above names, and each amendment carries its first edition beneath it. You amend `bible/power-system.md` in nothing but the one new section. You touch no controller file. You create no marker file. You introduce no new final enemy, no new cosmic layer, no new antagonist and no new world, and the antagonist ladder and the relationship milestones in `outline/series.md` are untouched, and the planned ending is untouched.**

**AND YOU CREATE EXACTLY ONE NEXT PHASE: `workspace/volume-12/batch-0001/PROMPT.md`. No continuation directory, no review prompt, no close prompt, no second batch prompt and no Volume 13 anything.**

## 12. The one phase you create, by path

**`workspace/volume-12/batch-0001/PROMPT.md`, and it is a BATCH and not an outline and not a close. It writes Chapters 0551 to 0560, days 551 to 560, one chapter to one day, and it decides nothing, invents no person, takes no descriptor, sends no notice, opens no notice, washes no wall above a board, puts nothing in a third column, fills no place on a form, asks no man of about fifty-seven anything, lifts no length of new rope, measures no fence, traces no mark, counts no days since anybody said no, uses no ordinal for a month, prints none of the strings named in §0, and derives the count of this city's silences in no file it produces.**

**AND IT WRITES ITS OWN TEN CARDS AT THE HEAD OF ITS OWN STATE RECORD BEFORE `chapters/volume-12/chapter-0551.md` EXISTS, BECAUSE THAT IS THE ARRANGEMENT AND IT APPLIES TO EVERY BATCH OF YOUR VOLUME INCLUDING THE ONE THAT FOLLOWS THE ONE YOU CREATE. It finds its own card file missing and stops and says so in its own record rather than writing a chapter — and the card file for that batch is written by you now, before Chapter 0551 exists, which is the one card file you write and the only one.**

**AND THE THINGS IT INHERITS FROM YOUR OWN PLAN, and this list is yours to fill: the days and the Bare-Month ordinals, the objects in its ten chapters, the protagonist's chapters and the two clauses §8 item 6 names, the pool, the pressure tags, the frames, the word-run rule, the two instruments, the eleven inherited debts, the five you paid and the six you declined, the questions it may not answer, and the string that is not on any page.**
